arxiv-2111-12699.title: Comparative analysis of the Compton ionization of Hydrogen and Positronium.
arxiv-2111-12699.creator: Ivan S. Stepantsov 1, Igor P. Volobuev 2 , Yuri V. Popov 2,3
arxiv-2111-12699.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ivan S. Stepantsov 1, Igor P. Volobuev 2 , Yuri V. Popov 2,3. The paper deals with the Compton disintegration of positronium and a comparison of the differential cross sections of this process with the similar cross sections in the case of the Compton ionization of the hydrogen atom. Special attention is paid to the resonances arising, when the electron and positron move parallel to each other in continuum states with the same velocities and zero relative momentum.

arxiv-2211-16700.title: AirCon: Over-the-Air Consensus for Wireless Blockchain Networks
arxiv-2211-16700.creator: Xin Xie, Cunqing Hua, Pengwenlong Gu, and Wenchao Xu
arxiv-2211-16700.description: Abstract Blockchain has been deemed as a promising solution for providing security and privacy protection in the next-generation wireless networks. Large-scale concurrent access for massive wireless devices to accomplish the consensus procedure may consume prohibitive communication and computing resources, and thus may limit the application of blockchain in wireless conditions.

arxiv-2212-01776.title: Notes on the complexity of coverings for Kronecker powers of symmetric matrices
arxiv-2212-01776.creator: Igor S. Sergeev
arxiv-2212-01776.description: Abstract In the present note, we study a new method of constructing efficient coverings for Kronecker powers of matrices, recently proposed by J. Alman, Y. Guan, A. Padaki [ 1 ] . We provide an alternative proof for the case of symmetric matrices in a stronger form.

arxiv-2212-11104.description: Abstract . We generalize Laurent monomials to toric quasifolds, a special class of highly singular spaces that extend simplicial toric varieties to the nonrational setting. Keywords. Toric variety, toric quasifold, nonrational fan, nonrational polytope, Laurent monomial Mathematics Subject Classification: 14M25, 52B20, 53D20. arxiv-2403-08667.description: Abstract . The space of chains on a compact connected space encodes all the different ways of continuously growing out of a point until exhausting the space. A chain is generic if its orbit under the action of the underlying homeomorphism group is comeager.

arxiv-2403-14756.title: Magnonic Superconductivity
arxiv-2403-14756.creator: Khachatur G. Nazaryan 1 , Liang Fu 1,∗ 1 Department of Physics, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, MA 02139 *Corresponding author: liangfu@mit.edu (L.F.)
arxiv-2403-14756.description: Abstract We uncover a superconducting state with partial spin polarization induced by a magnetic field. This state, which we call ”magnonic superconductor”, lacks a conventional pairing order parameter, but is characterized instead by a composite order parameter that represents the binding of electron pairs and magnons.

arxiv-2407-10558.title: ConTEXTure: Consistent Multiview Images to Texture
arxiv-2407-10558.creator: Jaehoon Ahn, Sumin Cho, Harim Jung, Kibeom Hong, Seonghoon Ban, Moon-Ryul Jung
arxiv-2407-10558.description: Abstract . We introduce ConTEXTure, a generative network designed to create a texture map/atlas for a given 3D mesh using images from multiple viewpoints. The process begins with generating a front-view image from a text prompt, such as ’Napoleon, front view’, describing the 3D mesh.

arxiv-2412-00944.title: Bilinear Convolution Decomposition for Causal RL Interpretability
arxiv-2412-00944.creator: Narmeen Oozeer, Sinem Erisken, Alice Rigg
arxiv-2412-00944.description: Abstract Efforts to interpret reinforcement learning (RL) models often rely on high-level techniques such as attribution or probing, which provide only correlational insights and coarse causal control. This work proposes replacing nonlinearities in convolutional neural networks (ConvNets) with bilinear variants, to produce a class of models for which these limitations can be addressed.

arxiv-2505-02622.title: PLS-completeness of string permutations
arxiv-2505-02622.creator: Dominik Scheder, Johannes Tantow
arxiv-2505-02622.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Dominik Scheder, Johannes Tantow. Bitstrings can be permuted via permutations and compared via the lexicographic order. In this paper we study the complexity of finding a minimum of a bitstring via given permutations. As a global optima is known to be NP -complete [ 1 ] , we study the local optima via the class PLS [ 8 ] and show hardness for PLS .

arxiv-2506-16303.title: Endoreversible Stirling cycles: plasma engines at maximal power
arxiv-2506-16303.creator: Gregory Behrendt, Sebastian Deffner
arxiv-2506-16303.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Gregory Behrendt, Sebastian Deffner. Endoreversible engine cycles are a cornerstone of finite-time thermodynamics. We show that endoreversible Stirling engines operating with a one-component plasma as working medium run at maximal power output with the Curzon-Ahlborn efficiency. As a main result, we elucidate that this is actually a consequence of the fact that the caloric equation of state depends only linearly on temperature and only additively on volume.

arxiv-2510-15134.title: FarsiMCQGen: a Persian Multiple-choice Question Generation Framework
arxiv-2510-15134.creator: Mohammad Heydari Rad, Rezvan Afari, Saeedeh Momtazi
arxiv-2510-15134.description: Abstract Multiple-choice questions (MCQs) are commonly used in educational testing, as they offer an efficient means of evaluating learners’ knowledge. However, generating high-quality MCQs, particularly in low-resource languages such as Persian, remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces FarsiMCQGen , an innovative approach for generating Persian-language MCQs.

pmc-11353879.title: Descriptive Study on the Relationship between Dyspnea, Physical Performance, and Functionality in Oncology Patients
pmc-11353879.creator: Diego Lucas-Ruano, Celia Sanchez-Gomez, María Isabel Rihuete-Galve, Alberto Garcia-Martin, Emilio Fonseca-Sanchez, Eduardo José Fernández-Rodríguez, Ana Cláudia Mesquita Garcia, Simone Yuriko Kameo, Namie Okino Sawada
pmc-11353879.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: Cancer is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality globally. Dyspnea, affecting up to 60% of cancer patients, exacerbates physical and psychological distress, reducing quality of life. This study aims to explore the relationship between dyspnea and factors such as age, sex, clinical diagnosis, and treatment lines in cancer patients, with the goal of improving understanding and management of this debilitating symptom to enhance patient care and quality of life.

pmc-11536223.title: Understanding the medication regimens associated with anticholinergic burden in older people's mental health services in the UK
pmc-11536223.creator: Thomas R E Barnes, Delia Bishara, Alistair Burns, Phyo K Myint, Olivia Rendora, Elena M Edokpolor Pernia, Carol Paton
pmc-11536223.description: BackgroundMedications with anticholinergic properties are associated with a range of adverse effects that tend to be worse in older people.AimsTo investigate medication regimens with high anticholinergic burden, prescribed for older adults under the care of mental health services.MethodClinical audit of prescribing practice, using a standardised data collection tool.

pmc-11663556.title: SYNTAXIN OF PLANTS 132 underpins secretion of cargoes associated with salicylic acid signaling and pathogen defense
pmc-11663556.creator: Sakharam Waghmare, Lingfeng Xia, Thu Phan Ly, Jing Xu, Sahar Farami, Richard Burchmore, Michael R Blatt, Rucha Karnik
pmc-11663556.description: Secretory trafficking in plant cells is facilitated by SNARE (soluble N-ethylmaleimide-sensitive factor attachment protein receptor) proteins that drive membrane fusion of cargo-containing vesicles. In Arabidopsis, SYNTAXIN OF PLANTS 132 (SYP132) is an evolutionarily ancient SNARE that functions with syntaxins SYP121 and SYP122 at the plasma membrane.

pmc-11692493.title: ARE WE WAREHOUSING PEOPLE WITH SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS? EXPLORING US NURSING HOMES IN 2000 AND 2021
pmc-11692493.creator: Kim Hadson, Marissa Bergh, Jasmine Travers
pmc-11692493.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The 1999 Supreme Court Olmstead decision reaffirmed people with serious mental illness (SMI) have the right to care integrated into community settings. The growth of SMI in nursing homes (NHs) suggests care has instead shifted to NHs. Insufficient attention has been given to the facility characteristics and state environments to understand if individuals with SMI in NHs are receiving high quality, equitable care.

pmc-11700655.title: Inhibition of proteolytic and ATPase activities of the proteasome by the BTK inhibitor CGI-1746
pmc-11700655.creator: Olasubomi A Akintola, Mitchell B Patterson, John G Smith, George N DeMartino, Amit K Mitra, Alexei F Kisselev
pmc-11700655.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). SummaryBruton’s tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitor, ibrutinib, has been shown to synergize in vitro with proteasome inhibitors (PIs) in reducing the viability of cells derived from B cell malignancies, but the mechanism is not known. We report here that an off-target effect of ibrutinib causes synergy because not all BTK inhibitors exhibited the synergistic effect, and those that synergized did so even in cells that do not express BTK. The allosteric BTK inhibitor CGI-1746 showed the strongest synergy.

pmc-12437000.title: Determinants of Deliberate COVID-19 Spread: Exploring Psychological, Social, and Environmental Factors Behind Virus-Spreading Behaviors During a Pandemic in Saudi Arabia
pmc-12437000.creator: S. Alsubaie, H. Alshahrani
pmc-12437000.description: IntroductionWhile most individuals adhere to preventive measures during pandemics, a subset engages in behaviors that may intentionally spread COVID-19, presenting unique challenges to public health efforts.ObjectivesThis study explores the psychological, social, and environmental factors influencing deliberate virus-spreading behavior in the Saudi Arabian population during the initial phase of the COVID-19 pandemic.

pmc-12641775.creator: Justyna Nowak, Agata Szymczak, Marta Morawska, Heli Kuusipalo, Emma Koivurinta, Kati Kuisma, Päivi Mäki, Taina Sainio, Nella Savolainen, Katarzyna Brukało

Material and method: Since March 2024, Poland has implemented Smart Family tools through training sessions for professionals who work or will work with families of children with excess body weight.

pmc-13128701.title: Dynamic tail amine interactions drive isoform selectivity for potent human neuronal nitric oxide synthase inhibitors
pmc-13128701.creator: Amardeep Awasthi, Koon Mook Kang, Richard B Silverman
pmc-13128701.description: Achieving isoform-selective inhibition of neuronal nitric oxide synthase (nNOS) remains a significant challenge due to the high structural similarity with other NOS isoforms. Here, we report the design, synthesis, and characterization of novel nNOS inhibitors 3 and 4, incorporating dimethylamino-substituted tail groups to exploit hnNOS-specific peripheral pocket interactions.

pmc-13377062.creator: Yang Wang, Zhiqiang Zhao, Hongtao Liu, Jinwen Hao, Xiaoxiang Wei

pmc-13430013.title: JNK and p53 cause human and mouse β cell death during excessive unfolded protein response
pmc-13430013.creator: Rohit B. Sharma, Christine Darko, Ying Wang, Thalia A. Castro, Tara Doma Lama, Brian Gablaski, Andrew Rappa, David Redmond, Jason K. Kim, Amy S. Lee, Laura C. Alonso
pmc-13430013.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress contributes to β cell death in both Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes (T1D and T2D). However, the molecular mechanisms driving β cell death during ER stress remain insufficiently defined, limiting development of protective therapies. GRP78, an ER chaperone, is the master regulator of unfolded protein response (UPR), suppressing UPR initiators during the unstressed state and releasing them to allow UPR activation during stress.

pmc-13525078.title: Empowerment of Youth With Intellectual Disabilities Through Inclusive Research in Africa
pmc-13525078.creator: Chioma Ohajunwa, Anthea Hansen, Lieketseng Ned, Theresa Lorenzo
pmc-13525078.description: BackgroundDespite growing global interest in participatory research, the practice of including persons with intellectual disabilities as co‐researchers remains largely underexplored within the African context. This paper reflects on the methodological processes of implementing inclusive research with youth with intellectual disabilities, including the lessons learned during this process.

pmc-13574560.title: Home-Based Cardiac Rehabilitation Using a Smart Ring and Telephone Counselling: A Randomized Controlled Trial
